int_name: N 5TH ST & W HUNTING PARK AVE

result.summary: The intersection features a wide roadway with a marked zebra crosswalk but lacks a pedestrian refuge island, resulting in a long exposure time for pedestrians. The environment is car-centric, dominated by industrial land use and wide travel lanes that likely encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross a wide expanse of roadway without a median or refuge island, increasing exposure to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway.

hazards.name: Wide Travel Lanes
hazards.description: The excessive width of the travel lanes can encourage higher vehicle speeds, increasing the risk and severity of potential collisions.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway extending into the background.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the crosswalk to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with basic pedestrian infrastructure, including a marked continental crosswalk and pedestrian signals. However, the wide roadway and parked vehicles near the crossing point increase pedestrian exposure and potentially obstruct sightlines between drivers and walkers.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection on the right side may obstruct the view of pedestrians for approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway near the crosswalk

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Cracking and wear in the asphalt within the crossing area could pose a minor trip hazard or affect accessibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce crossing distance and prevent parking too close to the crosswalk, improving sightlines.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment includes basic sidewalks and a marked crosswalk, but lacks robust traffic control or calming measures at the visible intersection. Visibility is hindered by parked vehicles along the curb, and the wide, uncontrolled roadway may facilitate higher vehicle speeds in a mixed-use area.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along the right side of the street block the view between pedestrians at the curb and oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway along the row houses

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop signs or signals are visible to regulate vehicle flow at the marked pedestrian crossing.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and uneven surfaces in the roadway can create tripping hazards or affect vehicle handling near the crossing.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the faded transverse markings to a continental or ladder pattern to increase visibility to approaching motorists.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and overhead traffic signals within a mixed-use urban environment. However, the lack of visible pedestrian-specific signals and the presence of parked vehicles near the crossing points create potential visibility and safety gaps for people walking.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners obstruct the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the main roadway approaching the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to clear sightlines.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.
